questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Fujian overtakes Zhejiang (+0.140 to 0.580; Zhejiang -0.105 to 0.395) ~48 hours before Saturday night July 11 mainland landfall as multi-agency tracks tighten around northern Fujian and the Min-Zhe border. On July 9 (18:00 CST), Bavi stood at 18.7N, 128.9E (1,030 km SE of Keelung, 52 m/s), with JTWC Warning #35 reporting 'tightly clustered' track guidance and high confidence through 72h (eliminating the far-north outlier spread). CMA/NMC Orange Alert holds landfall Saturday evening between Fuqing (Fujian, 25.7N) and Wenling (Zhejiang, 28.4N), with Reuters explicitly reporting CMA's forecast point as eastern Fujian province and Fuzhou Met (FZNews) narrowing the most likely core to Lianjiang (Fujian, 26.2N) through Cangnan (Zhejiang, 27.6N) — roughly two-thirds Fujian coastline relative to the 27.17N provincial border. NMFC's July 9 storm surge forecast independently confirms a center near northern Fujian (RED surge on Ningde and right-quadrant Wenzhou, ORANGE on Fuzhou, only YELLOW on Taizhou/Ningbo). Taiwan CWA issued its Sea Warning at 14:30 CST expecting Bavi to graze northern Taiwan waters (600-900mm mountain rain), whence a NW heading projects straight into Ningde/Xiapu/Fuding (Fujian) unless a 40-70 km northward deflection pushes landfall into Cangnan/Wenzhou (Zhejiang), justifying 39.5% for Zhejiang given ~90-110 km 48h track uncertainty. Tight clustering trims Shanghai (0.035 -> 0.015) and Jiangsu (0.015 -> 0.005), keeping Guangdong at 0.005. Sum = 1.000.

local_articles.title: 15 Killed In Philippines Landslide As Typhoon Bavi Nears Taiwan
local_articles.snippet: Fifteen people were killed in landslides in the Philippines, and more than 2,000 in Taiwan were evacuated from their homes, as the biggest typhoon in decades neared the region on Friday. Typhoon Bavi is expected to pound Taiwan's north and east, as well as Japan's remote southwestern islands, on Friday and Saturday before smashing into China, which has been hit by deadly storms this week. Two landslides triggered by heavy rains driven by Bavi killed at least 15 people and left six others missing on the Philippines' southern island of Mindanao, authorities said. Locals in Taiwan's port city of Keelung, which is expected to be one of the hardest hit areas on the island, stocked up on food, taped windows, and stacked sandbags along shop fronts, heeding warnings from authorities to take precautions. questions.background: Wimbledon is one of tennis's four Grand Slam tournaments and is played on grass in London.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official Wimbledon results identifying the 2026 women's singles champion. Resolution Date : The question resolves when the tournament officially confirms the winner of the 2026 women's singles final. Accepted Answer Format : The winning player's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Thursday July 9 Centre Court women's semifinals are complete, eliminating Coco Gauff (0.25) and Marta Kostyuk (0.265) and setting up the first all-Czech women's Grand Slam final on Saturday July 11 (4pm BST) between [10] Karolina Muchova and [9] Linda Noskova (Reuters, WTA, Straits Times). Muchova survived a 2h35m thriller in 33C heat, saving a match point to beat Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6(12-10) after beating Krejcikova and Osaka; Noskova cruised past Kostyuk 6-4, 6-4 in just 79 minutes (winning 76% 1st serves, 15/18 at net, and her last 3 matches in straight sets). Early July 9 sportsbook odds (MiCasino) open Muchova 1.77 (-130) vs Noskova 2.00 (+100), implying 53.05% / 46.95% vig-removed. Muchova holds a 1-0 H2H edge (2025 US Open R32, 6-7 6-4 6-2), a 10-match grass winning streak (including Bad Homburg), prior Slam final experience (2023 RG), and elite grass-court variety. Noskova counters strongly with tour-leading 19 grass wins over the past two years (11-1 in 2026 including Berlin title), dominant first-serve metrics (>70% won in 5 of 6 matches), and far greater freshness after Muchova showed third-set physical stiffness and took a hard diving volley fall in the tiebreak (mitigated by Friday's full rest day). Anchoring tightly to the market and H2H/experience vs freshness balance: Karolina Muchova 0.535, Linda Noskova 0.465 (sum = 1.000).

questions.title: Which ownership group will receive NFL owners' approval to buy the Seattle Seahawks in 2026?
questions.background: The Seattle Seahawks are owned by Paul Allen's estate. Allen's will calls for the team to be sold and the assets distributed to charities.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official NFL announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the purchasing group approved by NFL owners. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the purchasing ownership group in the first sale of the Seattle Seahawks formally approved by NFL owners during 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the purchasing group or the family leading it.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 9 breaking report from Front Office Sports (corroborated by NBC Sports, MyNorthwest, Spokesman-Review): following the June 29 first-round bid deadline, two front-runners have pulled ahead to buy the Seattle Seahawks — the Aditya Mittal and Wyc Grousbeck group (ArcelorMittal CEO / Celtics minority owner with >$17B family wealth + former Celtics governor who would operate the team part-time in Seattle) and the Vinod Khosla group (49ers 3.1% minority owner with ~$14B personal net worth, already NFL-vetted in May 2025, who would divest his 49ers stake). Crucially, FOS reports Todd Boehly is 'no longer in the running' (slashed -0.225 from 0.25 to 0.025 residual in case of re-entry/sourcing noise), Steve Apostolopoulos 'removed himself from the field' (dropped from top 5), and at least one unidentified bidder was eliminated, with one source saying it is down to just Mittal/Grousbeck and Khosla and expecting further news next month. Respecting anti-overconfidence on sourced reports AND FOS's explicit caution that a late billionaire could still swoop in (citing Steve Ballmer's 2014 Clippers bid, especially with Seahawks vice chair Bert Kolde, Roger Goodell, Robert Kraft, Jeff Bezos, Bill Gates, and Mark Zuckerberg attending Allen & Co's Sun Valley conference this week July 7-11), we allocate 0.80 combined to the two finalists (Mittal/Grousbeck slight favorite at 0.43 vs Khosla 0.37 on deeper combined capital + Grousbeck's championship operating track record, balanced by Khosla's existing NFL vetting and single-principal 30%-rule clarity), keep Jeff Bezos (0.03), Todd Boehly (0.025), and Steve Ballmer (0.02), and leave 12.5% unallocated (sum = 0.875) for any unnamed late entrant.

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 MotoGP German Grand Prix?
questions.background: This question concerns the premier-class main Grand Prix race, not the separate sprint race.
questions.resolution_criteria: Resolve to the rider classified as the winner of the 2026 German Grand Prix main race in the official MotoGP race results. Resolution occurs when the race classification is published. Provide the rider's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 3-7 German Grand Prix previews (MotoGP.com, GPBlog, Motorcycles.news, TodoCircuito) bring meaningful rider-fitness updates ahead of Friday July 10 Sachsenring practice. Marco Bezzecchi (trimmed 0.16 -> 0.13) is cleared to race but arrives 'battered and bruised' from his heavy Lap 2 Assen crash, with Aprilia Racing CEO Massimo Rivola publicly noting Bezzecchi 'definitely needs a break' amid four non-scores in five races. Nine-time Sachsenring MotoGP winner Marc Marquez (nudged 0.29 -> 0.31) confirmed his radial-nerve arm surgery six weeks ago ended fears of sudden arm failure and expects a stronger showing on Sachsenring's anti-clockwise, left-hand-dominated layout (where MotoGP.com tabs him double favorite despite Aprilia's 2026 pace). Championship leader and 2023 Sachsenring winner Jorge Martin moves slightly up (0.19 -> 0.20), third-in-standings top Ducati rider Fabio Di Giannantonio ticks up (0.07 -> 0.08), Assen winner Ai Ogura holds at 0.10, and injuries to rivals (Pedro Acosta fresh from carpal tunnel surgery, Maverick Vinales shoulder weakness, Johann Zarco and Fermin Aldeguer out) trim the outsider field to 18% (Raul Fernandez, 2024 winner Bagnaia, Alex Marquez, Acosta).
